universities.name: Slovak Medical University in Bratislava
universities.summary: Slovak Medical University in Bratislava, established in 2002 under the Ministry of Health of the Slovak Republic, runs a small, selective English-medium General Medicine programme leading to the MUDr degree. The university is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 2006 onward, and its accreditor, the Slovak Accreditation Agency for Higher Education, is recognized by the World Federation for Medical Education.
universities.campusLifestyle: The English-medium General Medicine track admits a deliberately small cohort of just 15 students per cycle, with admission ranked strictly by entrance-exam score up to that capacity. The programme's conditions are formally re-approved each year by the Faculty's Programme Council and Quality Council.
universities.cityProfile: Bratislava is Slovakia's capital. The university's clinical departments operate jointly with University Hospital Bratislava, reflected in named SMU clinics that are explicitly co-designated as SMU-and-University-Hospital-Bratislava joint departments.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS General Medicine programme combines theoretical and preclinical instruction with simulator-based and bedside clinical teaching. Clinical departments are co-located with University Hospital Bratislava, evidenced by named joint SMU-and-hospital clinics. Graduates receive the MUDr (Doktor Vseobecneho Lekarstva) degree, a Slovak state medical qualification carrying EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU and EEA.
universities.hostelOverview: The university's own 2026/27 admissions document states explicitly that Slovak Medical University does not provide accommodation for students in the English-language General Medicine programme; students on this track should budget for private rental housing in Bratislava. A separate general SMU accommodation page advertises a student dormitory with rates around EUR 135/bed/month during the academic year, but this may not extend to the English-track cohort given the programme-specific exclusion, so applicants should confirm directly with the university before relying on it.
universities.dietarySupport: Meals are available through the university's own cafeteria; no separate meal-plan cost is published.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. Admissions and student queries are handled through the Faculty's Pedagogical Department.
universities.studentSupport: Admissions correspondence is handled by the Faculty's Pedagogical Department (Pedagogicky odbor), reachable by mail at the university's Limbova 12 address in Bratislava.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0002854), currently operational, with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 2006 onward and Canadian medical-regulator acceptability noted in the same record.
Accreditation from the Slovak Accreditation Agency for Higher Education (SAAHE), a body recognized by the World Federation for Medical Education, most recently confirmed accredited on 6 March 2024.
The MUDr degree carries EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU and EEA as a Slovak state medical qualification.
A transparent, single-instrument admissions process: ranking is based solely on a 160-question Biology and Chemistry entrance exam, with no separate interview stage.
Clinical departments co-located with University Hospital Bratislava, a major public teaching hospital.
thingsToConsider: The university explicitly does not provide accommodation for English-track General Medicine students; budget for private rental housing in Bratislava.
Only 15 places are available per cycle, making this a small, competitive cohort by design.

The most recent admissions cycle (application deadline 31 May 2026, entrance exam 1 July 2026) has already closed as of this record's research date; the university has not yet published next-cycle dates.

No specific English-proficiency test score (such as IELTS or TOEFL) is stated as a requirement on the university's own official admissions document, despite some third-party sites claiming one -- confirm current language requirements directly with the university.
Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission NEET-UG Eligibility Certificate requirement; this is not referenced or administered by the university.
bestFitFor: Students confident preparing for a 160-question Biology and Chemistry entrance exam and comfortable with a small, highly selective cohort.
Applicants who have already arranged private accommodation in Bratislava, since the university does not provide housing for this programme.
Families prioritizing EU-wide licence recognition at a lower tuition point than many Western European medical schools.

faq.question: Is the General Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Admission requires completed secondary or secondary vocational education, with no prior university study required.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the MUDr degree, a Slovak state medical qualification listed under EU Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V for automatic recognition across the EU/EEA.

faq.question: How competitive is admission?
faq.answer: Only 15 places are offered per cycle in the English-medium track, and applicants are ranked strictly by their entrance-exam score up to that capacity.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: A 150-minute, 160-question multiple-choice exam covering Biology (80 questions) and Chemistry (80 questions), written in English, within secondary-school curriculum scope.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 10,000 per year, per the university's official 2026/27 admissions document, plus a separate, largely non-refundable EUR 70 admission fee (refundable only if the university does not open the programme due to low applicant numbers).

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: No. The university's official admissions document states explicitly that it does not provide accommodation for students in the English-language General Medicine programme; students should plan for private rental housing in Bratislava.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The most recent cycle had an application deadline of 31 May 2026 and an entrance exam on 1 July 2026; that cycle has closed, and the university had not yet published next-cycle dates at the time of research.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.
